prompts.business: Use TradeFlow MCP connection {{serverName}} ({{client}}). Its available tools are: {{tools}}. Query tools are read-only. Use staging tools only when I explicitly ask to record inbound or outbound transactions. Draft submissions remain pending human review and do not create formal records or change inventory; never describe them as completed transactions. First list available tools and run a minimal inventory query with {"page":1,"limit":5}. When a result has more pages, paginate with limit no greater than 100. For the requested date range, report the currency and FIFO costing basis returned by the tools. Then summarize this month’s sales, cost and profit by customer. If financial tools are unavailable, explain the account’s permissions instead of inventing numbers.
prompts.connect:
Configure this TradeFlow MCP connection in the Agent you are running in. Connection: {{client}} (account {{account}}) on {{server}}. Managed server name: {{serverName}}. Local profile: {{profile}}. Credential expires {{expiresAt}}. Transport: stdio bridge at {{helperPath}}. Launch command: {{serveCommand}}.

1. Use your own host’s current MCP management command or the configuration fields documented for the version you are actually running. Do not copy paths or field names from another host, and do not overwrite unrelated settings.
2. Register one local stdio server named {{serverName}} that runs the launch command above. The bridge reads the credential from its private profile and performs authentication, so do not add a token, Authorization header, or URL.
3. Preserve other MCP servers and comments. Ask me before editing project-level configuration instead of user-level configuration.
4. Trust or reload the connection as your host requires, then discover tools through your own MCP facilities and call get_inventory with {"page":1,"limit":5}. Report the validated limit and the row count.
5. If your host cannot run local stdio commands or cannot edit its own configuration, give me the exact manual steps and stop. Do not claim the connection works.

Do not open profile or credential files, print tokens or full configuration files, change file permissions, or disable host security checks. A service check does not prove the host loaded the connection.
prompts.update:
Synchronize my TradeFlow MCP connection {{client}} on {{server}} (account {{account}}, profile {{profile}}, server name {{serverName}}). Last known catalog version: {{catalogVersion}}; instruction guide: {{guideVersion}}. Known tools: {{tools}}.

1. Run the descriptor and read only its redacted JSON:
{{describeCommand}}
2. Re-discover the tools through the host’s MCP facilities so the host sees added, removed, renamed, or re-parameterized tools. If the host cannot refresh tools in the current session, tell me to reload or start a new session and stop after reporting.
3. Compare the discovered tools and input schemas with the known list. Report added, removed and changed tools, and update any TradeFlow usage instructions or skill the host supports to guide version {{guideVersion}}.
4. Call get_inventory with {"page":1,"limit":5} and report the validated limit and row count.
5. Do not reinstall the connection, re-issue the credential, or broaden permissions to obtain a missing tool. Report the account role and credential limits instead; I will review authorization in the connection assistant. Do not call transaction draft tools unless I explicitly ask.

Do not read credential files, print tokens or full configuration files, or change security settings.
prompts.repair:
Help diagnose my TradeFlow MCP connection {{client}} on {{server}} (account {{account}}, profile {{profile}}, server name {{serverName}}, credential expires {{expiresAt}}).

Run the diagnostic and read only its redacted JSON:
{{doctorCommand}}

It reports the service handshake, discovered tools and helper availability. It does not prove the host loaded the connection. Then check in order: (1) the host still has a stdio server named {{serverName}} that runs {{serveCommand}}; (2) the host was reloaded or the connection trusted after the last change; (3) a real tool call through the host, not just a direct probe; (4) credential expiry.

HTTP 401 or an expired or revoked credential requires me to renew it in the connection assistant. HTTP 403 requires checking my account role. HTTP 404 requires the backend MCP setting and reverse proxy. HTTP 429 requires waiting and respecting Retry-After. Network or TLS errors require restoring connectivity; never bypass certificate validation.

Do not read credential files, print tokens or full configuration, change account permissions, or disable host security. Report the failed step and whether a real host query succeeded.
